chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ayadi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Aban ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) who said:

There is no deed more superior on the Day of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha) than shedding blood (of the sacrificial animal), or walking in the goodness of one's parents, or visiting a relative with whom ties have been broken, giving them preference and greeting them first, or a man who feeds from the best of his sacrificial offering and invites to the remainder his neighbors, the orphans, the needy, and the slaves, and visits the imprisoned.

key_terms.دَمٍ مَسْفُوكٍ: Shedding blood (referring to the sacrificial animal)
key_terms.ذِي رَحِمٍ قَاطِعٍ: Relative with whom ties are broken
key_terms.صَالِحِ نُسُكِهِ: The best part of one's sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What are the five best deeds to perform on Eid al-Adha according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the convergence of ritual piety and social ethics, elevating practical acts of kindness—such as feeding the needy and visiting prisoners—to the same status as the primary sacrifice. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *birr al-walidayn* (kindness to parents) and *silat al-rahim* (kinship ties) as integral components of worship, particularly during the festive occasion of Eid al-Adha.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-69 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ayadi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Amr ibn Shimr, on the authority of Aban ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), “

Nothing is better than the following five on the day of Eid ul-Azha: offering (an animal); visiting one’s parents; re-establishing ties of kinship with those relatives with whom such ties are broken and being kind to them, greeting them and assisting them with one’s extra income; eating some of one’s own offering and feeding the rest to the orphans, the needy, the slaves and the helpless neighbors; visiting imprisoned persons and being kind to them.”
